title: The Industrial Revolution
text: The Industrial Revolution was the transition to new manufacturing processes in Europe and the United States, from roughly 1760 to 1840. Originating in Britain, it saw the shift from agricultural and handicraft economies to industries powered by machinery. Key innovations included the steam engine (improved by James Watt), the spinning jenny, the power loom, and iron smelting using coke instead of charcoal. The revolution transformed social structures, creating an industrial working class and expanding cities. It dramatically increased productive capacity and wealth but also led to poor working conditions, child labor, and environmental pollution. The Industrial Revolution laid the groundwork for modern capitalist economies.
